\midrule

\section*{Common PID Tuning Starting Points}
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{lccc}
\toprule
\textbf{Method} & $\boldsymbol{K_p}$ & $\boldsymbol{T_i}$ & $\boldsymbol{T_d}$ \\
\midrule
Ziegler-Nichols (P only) & $0.5\,K_u$ & --- & --- \\
Ziegler-Nichols (PI) & $0.45\,K_u$ & $P_u/1.2$ & --- \\
Ziegler-Nichols (PID) & $0.6\,K_u$ & $P_u/2$ & $P_u/8$ \\

\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
Where $K_u$ is the ultimate gain and $P_u$ is the ultimate period. These are starting points; always fine-tune experimentally.

\section*{Key Equations at a Glance}

\textbf{Ohm's Law}: $V = IR$. \textbf{Power}: $P = VI = I^2R = V^2/R$.

\textbf{Voltage divider}: $V_{\text{out}} = V_{\text{in}} \cdot R_2/(R_1 + R_2)$.

\textbf{RC time constant}: $\tau = RC$. \textbf{Cutoff frequency}: $f_c = 1/(2\pi RC)$.

\textbf{Nyquist criterion}: $f_s \geq 2 f_{\max}$ (practical: $f_s \geq 5$--$10 f_{\max}$).

\textbf{Quantization step}: $q = V_{\text{range}} / 2^n$. \textbf{ENOB}: $(\text{SINAD} - 1.76)/6.02$.

\textbf{INA128 gain}: $G = 1 + 49.4\,\text{k}\Omega / R_G$. At $G = 100$: $R_G = 499\,\Omega$. At $G = 603$: $R_G = 82\,\Omega$.

\textbf{Uncertainty propagation}: $u_f = \sqrt{\sum (\partial f/\partial x_i)^2 \cdot u_{x_i}^2}$.

\textbf{SNR}: $\text{SNR (dB)} = 20\log_{10}(V_{\text{signal}}/V_{\text{noise}})$.

\textbf{Gain (dB)}: $20\log_{10}(V_{\text{out}}/V_{\text{in}})$. $+6$\,dB $= 2\times$. $-3$\,dB $= 0.707\times$. $-20$\,dB $= 0.1\times$.

\textbf{PID}: $u(t) = K_p\left[e(t) + \frac{1}{T_i}\int e\,dt + T_d\frac{de}{dt}\right]$.

\textbf{Phase lag from latency}: $\phi = -360 \cdot f \cdot \tau_{\text{total}}$ (degrees).

\textbf{Biot number}: $Bi = hL_c/k$. Lumped capacitance valid if $Bi < 0.1$.

\textbf{Thermal time constant}: $\tau = mC_p/(hA_s)$.

\textbf{Steady-state temperature}: $T_{ss} = T_{\text{amb}} + \dot{Q}/(hA)$.
